passage:
Class10B Girls (group chat)
Rohini: did u see Nikita's voice note lol
Sanya: screenshotting this
Sanya: she sounds so fake
Nikita: that was private!! who shared it
Rohini: relax it's a joke
(Someone forwards the screenshots to the whole grade.)

Nikita to Tanuja (private)
Nikita: everyone has it. I can't breathe
Tanuja: Don't reply to them. I mean it.
Tanuja: Screenshot everything, names and times. Mute the chat.
Nikita: I want to scream at them
Tanuja: I know. That's what they want. It's not your fault
Tanuja: Tell Ms Rao tomorrow and show her the screenshots. I'll come with you

qa.q: Whose voice note started the pile-on in the group chat?
How is Nikita feeling in her private chat with Tanuja?
qa.a: Panicked and exposed. She says everyone has it, that she cannot breathe and that she wants to scream at them.

qa.q: What advice does Tanuja give that would help Nikita?
qa.a: Not to reply in anger, to screenshot everything with names and times, to mute the chat and to tell Ms Rao with the screenshots.

qa.q: How does Tanuja seem to see what is happening?
qa.a: Tanuja sees a pile-on that is not Nikita's fault and that Nikita should not feed, and offers to go with Nikita to Ms Rao.

grounding: A group chat turns on Nikita and screenshots circulate; she is told not to reply in anger and to save evidence, mute and tell a teacher.

passage:
Tuesday night
I don't even know how to write this. This afternoon, someone screenshotted what I wrote in the class group about the science project, and cropped it so it looked like I was insulting Meghna. Then it was everywhere. Thirty-two messages in an hour. People I've never spoken to calling me fake. Someone made a sticker of my face.
I felt sick. My hands shook so much I dropped my phone. I wanted to reply to everyone, explain, shout. I typed a long message and then didn't send it.
Instead, I did what the cyber-safety poster in school says. I took screenshots of everything, with names and times. I muted the group.
Then I told Mummy and Chetan bhaiya at dinner. Mummy read it all, hugged me, and said, "Indu, this is not your fault." She emailed my class teacher tonight, and we're meeting the teacher at eight tomorrow.
I still feel exposed. But I'm not alone in it.

qa.q: How many messages were posted in an hour?
How did Indu feel when the screenshot spread?
qa.a: Indu felt sick, panicked and exposed, with hands shaking and a strong urge to reply and explain.

qa.q: Which steps helped Indu, and why?
qa.a: Not replying in anger, saving screenshots, muting the group, and telling Mummy the same day, so adults could act.

qa.q: How does Mummy respond when Indu tells her?
qa.a: Mummy reads everything, hugs Indu, says it isn't Indu's fault, and emails the class teacher that same night.

grounding: A teen targeted by a group chat pile-on avoids angry replies, saves evidence, mutes the chat and tells a trusted adult the same day.

qa.q: What were they saying Aadhya copied?
How was Aadhya feeling when she saw the section group?
qa.a: She felt panicked and exposed, unable to stop shaking, and wanted to scream at everyone.

qa.q: What steps did Parveen help Aadhya take, and why?
qa.a: Not replying, saving evidence, muting the group and calling her mum right away, which brought in adult help the same day.

grounding: A teen facing a group chat pile-on doesn't reply in anger, saves evidence, mutes the chat and tells her mother the same day.
